correctness.rationale: Connectedness and B>0 give a positive definite grounded Laplacian throughout the simplex. For a nonzero diagonal variation D the Hessian quadratic form is 2||A^(-1/2) D A^(-1)||_F²>0, so the minimizer is unique and invariant under both class permutation groups. The two contrast eigenspaces and the quotient on partwise constants give the stated trace. With b=(B−pa)/q, differentiation gives q² f'_B(0)=F_{p,q}(t) and f'_B(B/p)=2/B+1/p−(p−1)/(p+q+B/p)²>0. Strict convexity proves the criterion including equality. The turning point of h_β=(β+2/t)(1+t)² is its unique positive critical point, βt₀²+t₀=1; its minimum and divergence at both ends prove the support classification. For p=2 and q≤5, α≤10<Γ(1)≤Γ(β), while q=6 gives F(1/2)=53/48 and the stated cubic, whose positive roots agree with the displayed decimals. For q/p^(3/4)→c, the difference α−β is 2c³p^(1/4)+o(p^(1/4)), whereas Γ−β is 4cp^(1/4)+o(p^(1/4)); this proves the crossover away from c=√2. For fixed p, α→∞ and β→p force the two roots to zero and infinity; the leading balances give the stated transition budget scales. The two size limits are different; neither resolves the critical joint scaling layer.

originality.rationale: The inverse-trace optimization itself is already present as a special case of an existing convex relaxation. The strongest distinct indexed exact result shares reentrance, the q=6 onset for two hubs and both leading budget scales, but it concerns K₂,ᵩ without the hub edge and has different exact thresholds. The supported distinct contribution is the general split-graph closed support inequality, budget-window classification and growing-clique three-quarter-power law, not the general optimization or the existence of hub reentrance in any network.
residual_risks: A broader unindexed exact allocation theorem could cover weighted split networks and their support thresholds. The bounded comparison does not certify priority or same-day ordering.

value.rationale: For a natural continuous-actuation variance objective, it matters whether to devote nothing to an entire well-connected orbit as available actuation increases. The exact budget window and nontrivial moving-size threshold answer this without repeated optimization runs. The asymptotic constants for two hubs overlap prior bipartite behavior; the varying-p classification and 3/4 crossover provide structural value beyond adding one edge or reporting numerical optima.
